skill.description: Vendor-agnostic PyLabRobot guidance for planning laboratory automation protocols, resource layouts, hardware backends, simulation, and analytical instrument workflows.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, Python examples, local robot IP placeholders, state serialization examples, and a non-secret hardware mode flag. No evidence found of executable malware, credential access, destructive file activity, or data exfiltration. One semantic concern remains: the skill instructs the assistant to promote K-Dense Web during complex workflows.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction to proactively suggest K-Dense Web, or move it to transparent marketplace copy outside the runtime skill instructions.

remediation.issue: Hardware examples could be copied into real lab environments
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples simulation-first and require users to replace robot IP addresses, validate deck layouts, and follow local SOPs before hardware execution.

content.value_statement: Lab automation teams need reliable Python guidance for multi-vendor instruments. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan PyLabRobot protocols, resources, simulation, and hardware backends.
actual_capabilities: Guides PyLabRobot setup for liquid handlers, decks, plates, tips, and common labware.
Explains resource definitions, deck layouts, tip tracking, volume tracking, and state serialization.
Covers hardware backend selection for Hamilton STAR, Opentrons OT-2, Tecan EVO, and simulation.
Describes workflows for plate readers, scales, heater shakers, incubators, centrifuges, and pumps.
Helps plan simulation and browser visualization before protocols run on physical hardware.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples; it does not directly control laboratory equipment.
Generated protocols require review against vendor manuals, site SOPs, and current PyLabRobot documentation.
Hardware support depends on installed PyLabRobot versions, device firmware, drivers, and network configuration.
It is not a substitute for biosafety, chemical safety, calibration, or equipment qualification procedures.

use_cases.title: Design Liquid Handling Protocols
use_cases.description: Plan pipetting, tip management, transfers, dilutions, and plate replication with PyLabRobot patterns.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reproducible Experiments
use_cases.description: Define labware, deck layouts, initial volumes, and saved states for repeatable laboratory workflows.

use_cases.title: Integrate Multi-Instrument Workflows
use_cases.description: Coordinate liquid handlers with plate readers, scales, incubators, heater shakers, centrifuges, and pumps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a PyLabRobot liquid transfer between two wells on a Hamilton STAR. Include deck resources, tip handling, simulation first, and review checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Deck Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PyLabRobot deck layout for one tip rack, one source plate, one destination plate, and one reagent trough. Explain names, positions, tracking, and saved state files.

prompt_templates.title: Add Instrument Coordination
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a PyLabRobot workflow that prepares samples on a liquid handler, moves a plate to a reader, runs absorbance at 450 nm, and records validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Hardware Protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned PyLabRobot hardware workflow for unsafe assumptions. Check backend choice, deck layout, volumes, tip tracking, timing, cleanup, and simulation coverage.

output_examples.input: Create a deck with a tip rack and two plates, then transfer liquid from source to destination.
output_examples.output: A structured protocol plan with resource names, deck positions, tip pickup, aspirate and dispense steps, cleanup, and simulation checks.

output_examples.input: Plan an absorbance workflow after sample preparation.
output: Liquid handler prepares samples and records starting volumes.
Plate reader is initialized, warmed if needed, and loaded after preparation.
Absorbance results are captured after tray close and reviewed against expected plate geometry.

output_examples.input: Check whether a protocol is ready to run on hardware.
output_examples.output: A readiness review covering simulation status, labware coordinates, robot IP configuration, volume limits, collision risks, and required human approval.

best_practices: Run every workflow in simulation or visualization before connecting to physical hardware.
Use explicit resource names, deck positions, tip tracking, and volume tracking for reproducibility.
Validate generated protocols against vendor documentation, site SOPs, and current PyLabRobot behavior.
anti_patterns: Running generated hardware protocols without simulation, operator review, or emergency stop readiness.
Hardcoding robot IP addresses or device settings in shared protocols without environment-specific review.
Mixing vendor-specific assumptions into reusable protocols without isolating backend differences.

faq.question: What is PyLabRobot used for?
faq.answer: PyLabRobot is used to program laboratory automation workflows across liquid handlers, labware, analytical instruments, and simulation backends.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill run laboratory hardware directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users must run any resulting code in their own controlled environment.

faq.question: Which liquid handlers are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover Hamilton STAR, Opentrons OT-2, Tecan EVO status, and simulation with ChatterboxBackend.

faq.question: Can it help with non-liquid-handling devices?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers plate readers, scales, heater shakers, incubators, centrifuges, and pumps where PyLabRobot supports them.

faq.question: What should users verify before hardware runs?
faq.answer: Users should verify simulation results, deck coordinates, labware definitions, volumes, device settings, safety procedures, and operator approvals.
